claims.text: BPH is proliferation of glandular and stromal tissue in the prostate transition zone
claims.quote: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) refers to the proliferation of glandular and stromal components within the transition zone of the prostate.

claims.text: LUTS can come from the bladder, prostate, urethra or other causes
claims.quote: Non-neurogenic lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) can be due to bladder, prostate, urethral, or other pathology.

claims.text: Systematic review searched through January 2025 with update searches December 15, 2025
claims.quote: searches in Ovid MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews through January 2025. Update searches were conducted on December 15, 2025.

claims.text: Part I covers history, physical exam, appropriate use of tests and counseling; history, exam and tests come before treatment
claims.quote: In addition to patient history and physical examination, the recommendations herein include the appropriate use of tests and patient counseling.

claims.text: Bothersome symptoms drive management; shared decision-making is critical in starting and stepping up treatment
claims.quote: Bothersome LUTS is the main reason patients seek treatment and generally drives management decisions. As such, shared decision-making plays a critical role in the initiation and escalation of treatment.

claims.text: BPH growth is not caused by cancer
claims.quote: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a condition in which the prostate gland grows larger than normal, but the growth is not caused by cancer.

claims.text: Second growth phase starts around age 25 and continues throughout life
claims.quote: The second growth phase starts around age 25 and continues throughout life.

claims.text: BPH affects 5% to 6% of men 40 to 64 and 29% to 33% of men 65 and older
claims.quote: Experts estimate that BPH affects 5% to 6% of men ages 40 to 64 and 29% to 33% of those ages 65 and older.

claims.text: Most common prostate problem over 50; rarely causes symptoms before 40
claims.quote: BPH is the most common prostate problem in men older than age 50. ... BPH rarely causes symptoms in men younger than age 40.

claims.text: Risk factors: family history, heart and blood vessel disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, ED, physical inactivity
claims.quote: have a family history of BPH ... have certain conditions such as heart and blood vessel disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease, or erectile dysfunction (ED) ... are not physically active

claims.text: No known prevention; being physically active may help reduce risk
claims.quote: Researchers have not found a way to prevent BPH, but being physically active may help reduce your risk.

claims.text: Get care right away for inability to urinate, blood in urine, or painful frequent urgent urination with fever and chills
claims.quote: Tell a health care professional right away if you cannot urinate at all ... feel painful, frequent, and urgent needs to urinate, and have a fever and chills ... have blood in your urine

claims.text: Having an enlarged prostate is not thought to raise prostate cancer risk
claims.quote: Having an enlarged prostate is not thought to raise the risk of getting prostate cancer.

claims.text: If you cannot pass any urine, get medical help right away
claims.quote: If you can't pass any urine, get medical help right away.

claims.text: LUTS from BPH affect 38.1 million U.S. men older than 30, about one in four
claims.quote: affect 38.1 million men older than 30 years in the United States, about one-fourth of all U.S. men

claims.text: about two of every three men 50 or older
claims.quote: lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH affecting approximately two of every three men 50 years or older

claims.text: Alpha blockers bring rapid improvement vs placebo, based on 19 RCTs with nearly 10,000 participants
claims.quote: Use of alpha-blockers leads to rapid improvement in lower urinary tract symptoms compared with placebo, based on 19 randomized controlled trials with nearly 10,000 participants

claims.text: 5-ARIs can take up to a year for full effect; started for uncontrolled symptoms when prostate is 30 mL or more by ultrasound
claims.quote: For uncontrolled symptoms, 5-alpha reductase inhibitors should be started if the prostate volume is 30 mL or greater by ultrasonography. 5-Alpha reductase inhibitors take up to one year to be fully beneficial

claims.text: Of men treated for LUTS from BPH, about 1% have a procedure or surgery
claims.quote: Of men who are treated for lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH, 1% have a procedural or surgical intervention.

claims.text: Risk factors: hypertension associated with more LUTS and larger prostates; lack of daily walking associated with progression; sedentary lifestyle, hypertension, diabetes increase risk
claims.quote: Hypertension is associated with more lower urinary tract symptoms and larger prostate volumes. ... Lack of daily walking is associated with progression in lower urinary tract symptoms.

claims.text: Sedentary lifestyle, hypertension and diabetes increase risk of symptoms
claims.quote: Sedentary lifestyle, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus increase risk of symptoms.

claims.text: IPSS is the best way to track symptoms; only symptom score to significantly predict urinary retention; 20 or higher indicates severe symptoms
claims.quote: The International Prostate Symptom Score is the best way to track symptoms. ... it is the only symptom score to significantly predict urinary retention ... An IPSS of 20 or higher, demonstrating severe lower urinary tract symptoms

claims.text: PSA testing not recommended in routine LUTS evaluation; shared decision-making for screening
claims.quote: Serum prostate-specific antigen testing is not recommended in routine evaluation of lower urinary tract symptoms, and shared decision-making should be used for cancer screening decisions.

claims.text: PAE evidence for main outcomes rated low or very low certainty
claims.quote: low or very low certainty of evidence for these main outcomes

claims.text: Decision table: self-management (evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol, toilet and bladder training) for mild symptoms; low- to moderate-quality evidence
claims.quote: Self-management methods, including limiting evening fluid intake, reducing caffeine and alcohol intake, toilet and bladder training, pelvic floor exercises, and mindfulness techniques, can improve symptoms.

claims.text: Low- to moderate-quality evidence that self-management improves symptoms
claims.quote: Low- to moderate-quality evidence suggests improvement in symptoms with self-management techniques

claims.text: Primary medical treatment: alpha blocker or PDE5 inhibitor
claims.quote: Primary medical treatment involves alpha blockers or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.

claims.text: Alpha blocker plus 5-ARI more effective than either alone after more than one year; no difference at one year or less
claims.quote: is more effective than either medication alone after more than one year ... However, at one year or less, no difference occurs.

claims.text: Acute urinary retention: start alpha blocker at catheterization, treat three days before catheter removal
claims.quote: For patients with acute urinary retention, immediately start an alpha blocker at urinary catheterization ... treat the patient for three days before attempting to remove the catheter.

claims.text: Poor control or complications (retention, recurrent UTI, renal insufficiency, recalcitrant gross hematuria) and other reasons to consider procedures
claims.quote: signs of poor control such as renal insufficiency, urinary retention, recurrent urinary tract infections, or recalcitrant gross hematuria ... failure of lifestyle interventions and medical therapy, a desire to avoid daily medications, intolerable adverse effects

claims.text: DRE reliably identifies only prostates larger than 50 mL; limited accuracy for size
claims.quote: reliably identifies only prostates larger than 50 mL ... Rectal examination has limited accuracy in evaluating prostate size.

claims.text: Sitting while urinating reduces post-void volume (low-quality evidence)
claims.quote: Low-quality evidence suggests that sitting while urinating reduces postvoid urinary volume.

claims.quote: avoid alpha blockers until ophthalmologist evaluation because of associated floppy iris syndrome

claims.quote: Decreased volume of prostate by 15% to 25% at six months based on three RCTs with nearly 4,000 men

claims.text: AUA recommends 5-ARIs if prostate volume 30 mL or greater on imaging
claims.quote: if prostate volume is 30 mL or greater on imaging
